prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The wirelength model's gamma schedule is the single strongest lever on how tightly cells cluster (small gamma = HPWL-like, strong pull; large gamma = diffuse). Making the overflow→gamma coefficient less aggressive at low overflow keeps the model closer to HPWL early (denser, shorter critical nets) and only diffuses when congestion is really high, which should shorten many moderate paths and reduce TNS on all circuits.
Rule-based digest:
total=-0.030 robust(mean-std)=-0.074 min_case=-0.061 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=-0.061 dWNS=-1.3% dTNS=-9.2% overflow~111
  bp-ng45: score=-0.048 dWNS=-7.0% dTNS=-3.4% overflow~139
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.080 dWNS=+13.8% dTNS=+4.3% overflow~165
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Hypothesis partly failed: total score −0.030, robust −0.074, with 2 of 3 cases worse. Ariane133-ng45 (dTNS −9.2%) and bp-ng45 (dWNS −7.0%) regressed, while bp_fe-ng45 improved (+13.8% WNS, +4.3% TNS). Mechanism: keeping gamma HPWL-like early densifies cells, but at overflow ~111–139 this likely over-congests moderate paths, hurting TNS; only the higher-overflow case (165) benefited from delayed diffusion. Next step: make the overflow→gamma coefficient overflow-adaptive with a threshold near 150, so densification persists only below it, and re-test across seeds.
